diagrams.title: From Seller Mandate to Earned Commission
diagrams.subtitle: Five documented handoffs keep equipment principal outside broker revenue.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The operator acts as a broker, not an inventory owner. Contract terms define commission entitlement, settlement instructions, inspection scope, and each party's responsibilities. Stage numbers indicate sequence rather than money or conversion.
diagrams.caption: Use one transaction identifier across the mandate, serial-number evidence, lien work, buyer acceptance, and escrow statement. Recognize only the earned broker commission; never classify equipment purchase funds as operating revenue.

stages.label: Authorize the mandate
stages.value: Verify seller identity, authority, asset, and commission terms
stages.detail: Obtain a signed seller mandate naming the legal owner, machine serial number or VIN, asking price, commission formula, term, and authority to advertise. Independently verify the signer's authority before distributing inventory.

stages.label: Build the evidence packet
stages.value: Inspect condition and separate measurements from seller claims
stages.detail: Collect service history, hour-meter evidence, ownership documents, and an independent inspection. For CNC assets, record controller version, spindle condition, tooling inclusions, power requirements, and loading constraints.

stages.label: Resolve ownership and liens
stages.value: Document creditor payoff and asset-specific release mechanics
stages.detail: Search under the correct debtor identity and jurisdiction; check certificate-of-title records where applicable. Under UCC 9-315, a security interest can survive sale. Obtain secured-party authorization and the required release documents rather than treating a search result as clearance.

stages.label: Match and contract the buyer
stages.value: Confirm purchasing authority, acceptance terms, and funded capacity
stages.detail: Use Airtable inventory fields and HubSpot buyer alerts to match capacity, location, budget, and timing. Document inspection acceptance, seller representations, rigging responsibility, delivery terms, and the commission trigger.

stages.label: Settle and reconcile
stages.value: Release funds against agreed evidence and book commissions only
stages.detail: Use an independent escrow provider appropriate to the transaction. Verify changed wire instructions through a previously verified phone number. Reconcile buyer funds, creditor payoff, seller proceeds, broker commission, and delivery evidence to the signed settlement statement.

diagrams.title: A Nested Annual Funnel to $450,000
diagrams.subtitle: Follow equipment opportunities through five increasingly qualified cohorts.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative annual Base-Case planning cohort, not observed conversion data. Every count represents equipment opportunities from the same original 500-record cohort, deduplicated by owner and asset identifier. Assume 30 settled transactions, each at $250,000 equipment value and a 6% broker commission.
diagrams.caption: 500 × 40% × 50% × 50% × 60% = 30 settlements. 30 × $15,000 = $450,000 recognized broker revenue. The corresponding $7,500,000 equipment transaction value belongs outside revenue. The 6% overall conversion is a planning assumption.

stages.label: Screened seller opportunities
stages.value: 500 distinct equipment opportunities enter the annual cohort
stages.detail: Record owner identity, asset identifier, equipment class, location, and disposition timing. Remove duplicate listings before calculating any conversion rate.

stages.label: Signed broker mandates
stages.value: 200 opportunities retain documented seller authority and pricing
stages.detail: Convert 40% of the original cohort into signed mandates with commission terms, evidence access, and a plausible asking price; retain rejected reasons in the CRM.

stages.label: Qualified buyer matches
stages.value: 100 mandated opportunities secure credible buyer engagement
stages.detail: Convert 50% of mandated opportunities into buyer-matched assets. Require named purchasing authority, suitable capacity requirements, and a credible funding path; email opens do not qualify.

stages.label: Diligence-ready transactions
stages.value: 50 matched opportunities reach documented diligence readiness
stages.detail: Convert 50% of buyer-matched opportunities after inspection scheduling, ownership review, negotiated commercial terms, and a documented settlement route.

stages.label: Settled commission events
stages.value: 30 transactions generate fifteen thousand dollars each
stages.detail: Convert 60% of diligence-ready opportunities into settlements satisfying the contractual commission trigger. Retain failed inspection, lien, funding, and timing outcomes rather than deleting lost opportunities.

diagrams.title: $450,000 Commissions to $157,500 Owner Net
diagrams.subtitle: Six bars reconcile the canonical Base-Case 35.0% net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Annual USD. Opening revenue and closing owner net are total bars; the four intervening values are negative expense movements. Expense allocations illustrate a reconciliation, not supplied scorecard line items. Contractor fees and deal-variable costs are separate from the recurring operating-overhead budget.
diagrams.caption: $450,000 − $120,000 − $72,000 − $48,000 − $52,500 = $157,500; $157,500 / $450,000 = 35.0%. Recurring overhead is $4,000 monthly, within the canonical $2,500–$14,000 monthly range; total annual expenses also include variable deal costs. Equipment principal never enters this bridge.

stages.label: Gross broker commissions
stages.value: $450,000 annual revenue from earned broker commissions
stages.detail: Opening total: 30 illustrative settlements at $15,000 commission each. Do not add the $7,500,000 underlying equipment value, escrow deposits, or creditor payoffs to this revenue figure.

stages.label: Contractor execution
stages.value: Subtract $120,000 for contracted delivery and transaction support
stages.detail: Budget contractor sourcing, coordination, and routine inspection labor across the three-contractor Base pod. Resulting balance: $330,000. Contractor status must follow actual working arrangements rather than the seat label.

stages.label: External deal services
stages.value: Subtract $72,000 for incremental specialist and closing services
stages.detail: Budget outside diagnostics, equipment-specific specialist reports, title work, and deal travel borne by the broker. Exclude labor already counted in contractor execution and transport paid directly by buyers. Balance: $258,000.

stages.label: Recurring operating overhead
stages.value: Subtract $48,000 for twelve months of operating infrastructure
stages.detail: Allocate $4,000 monthly to CRM, inventory matching, buyer alerts, insurance, bookkeeping, and communications. This is the recurring overhead component, not the total monthly equivalent of every expense. Balance: $210,000.

stages.label: Acquisition and settlement friction
stages.value: Subtract $52,500 for acquisition, settlement fees, and losses
stages.detail: Illustratively allocate $30,000 to buyer and seller acquisition, $12,000 to broker-borne settlement charges, and $10,500 to realized claim or collection losses. Count each expense once. Resulting balance: $157,500.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.value: $157,500 owner net equals thirty-five percent of revenue
stages.detail: Closing total, not an additional upward movement. Preserve the canonical owner-net definition: no extra owner salary or personal tax adjustment is introduced. Conservative remains $100,000 × 25% = $25,000; Scaled remains $800,000 × 45% = $360,000.

diagrams.title: Compare Commission Yield, Not Equipment Value
diagrams.subtitle: Five illustrative sub-niche yields use the same $100,000 sale denominator.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are commission percentages, not dollars, net margins, or published market averages. Each bar assumes a $100,000 equipment sale solely to isolate yield. Actual commission schedules depend on mandate scope and negotiation; these bars do not replace canonical annual scenarios.
diagrams.caption: At a common $100,000 sale value, an 8% commission earns $8,000 and a 3% commission earns $3,000. Compare inspection effort, sales-cycle length, claim exposure, and collection reliability before choosing a niche. Escrow protects settlement mechanics; it does not establish equipment condition.

stages.label: Specialized industrial equipment
stages.value: 8% illustrative yield earns eight thousand dollars
stages.detail: Assume a scarce, specification-sensitive asset with a narrow buyer pool. Verify utilities, controls, guarding, and removal scope; higher assumed commission yield can be consumed by specialist diligence and slow matching.

stages.label: CNC machine tools
stages.value: 6% illustrative yield earns six thousand dollars
stages.detail: Require serial-specific configuration, controller and spindle evidence, service records, and independent condition review. This 6% assumption also supports the separate Base funnel's $250,000 average equipment sale.

stages.label: Heavy construction equipment
stages.value: 5% illustrative yield earns five thousand dollars
stages.detail: Check hour-meter consistency, hydraulic condition, undercarriage wear, attachment ownership, and lien exposure. Document inspection limits where equipment cannot be tested under working load.

stages.label: Warehouse and material-handling assets
stages.value: 4% illustrative yield earns four thousand dollars
stages.detail: Verify rated capacity, mast configuration, battery condition, charger inclusion, and service evidence. Separate broker compensation from freight and loading charges paid directly to service providers.

stages.label: Commercial fleet vehicles
stages.value: 3% illustrative yield earns three thousand dollars
stages.detail: Check VIN, certificate of title, recorded lienholder, mileage evidence, and state dealer or broker licensing requirements. Reject payment from an unrelated party until identity and transaction purpose are resolved.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Advertising or Releasing Funds
diagrams.subtitle: Each unresolved branch has a specific stop condition and corrective action.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Four ordered decision nodes; numeric values indicate check sequence. Apply the relevant state's enacted UCC and licensing rules. Cornell UCC text is a reference model, not a substitute for identifying the controlling state enactment.
diagrams.caption: Pass each check with retained evidence. Missing license coverage halts regulated activity; unresolved ownership halts settlement; unsupported condition claims halt publication; unresolved export restrictions halt the affected transaction or shipment.

stages.label: Activity and licensing
stages.value: Proceed only after classifying asset, jurisdiction, and brokerage activity
stages.detail: Determine whether the activity requires a dealer, vehicle broker, auction, or other state authorization. California Vehicle Code section 11700 is a vehicle dealer example, not a universal CNC licensing rule. If required coverage is absent, stop that activity until the required authorization is effective.

stages.label: Ownership and lien release
stages.value: Proceed only with verified ownership and executable creditor releases
stages.detail: Apply UCC 9-315 and the applicable title regime. Obtain a payoff statement and asset-specific release or sale authorization from the secured party. Use an authorized UCC-3 amendment or termination under UCC 9-513 as appropriate; do not terminate a broader facility merely because one machine is being sold.

stages.label: Condition and warranties
stages.value: Proceed only with supportable descriptions and explicit contract allocation
stages.detail: Review seller descriptions, inspection findings, and contract language against applicable UCC 2-312, 2-313, and 2-316. Identify the seller and the broker's authority. Pause unsupported claims; a general as-is statement does not automatically erase an express warranty.

stages.label: Export and payment integrity
stages.value: Proceed only after resolving classification, counterparties, and settlement risks
stages.detail: For export transactions, determine EAR scope under 15 CFR Part 734, classification and destination controls under Part 738, and restrictions under Parts 744 and 746; also assess applicable OFAC sanctions under 31 CFR Chapter V. Resolve required authorizations before shipment and independently verify escrow and wire instructions before releasing funds.

diagrams.title: Four Base Seats; Six People at Scale
diagrams.subtitle: One full-time owner and three contractors divide commercial and evidence work.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each numeric value represents one person in the four-person Conservative and Base pod: 1 FT + 3 C. Contractor seats represent assigned responsibilities, not necessarily full-time workloads. Scaled expands to 2 FT + 4 C by adding one full-time commercial operator and one contractor inspection specialist.
diagrams.caption: Conservative: $100,000 revenue and $25,000 owner net with 1 FT + 3 C. Base: $450,000 revenue and $157,500 owner net with the same four people. Scaled: $800,000 revenue and $360,000 owner net with 2 FT + 4 C. The upper revenue scenario uses six people, not the four-person Base pod.

stages.label: Owner and commercial lead
stages.value: One full-time seat owns mandates, pricing, and broker revenue
stages.detail: Own seller qualification, buyer negotiation, signed mandates, and commission collection. Review exceptions without personally controlling every evidence source. At scale, add a second full-time commercial operator to split seller development and buyer conversion.

stages.label: Technical inspection specialist
stages.value: One contractor seat owns independent equipment condition evidence
stages.detail: Produce serial-specific inspection reports, photograph defects, document test limitations, and estimate repair scope separately from sale pricing. Add a second contractor inspection specialist at scale to expand equipment coverage and reduce scheduling bottlenecks.

stages.label: Inventory and buyer research analyst
stages.value: One contractor seat owns inventory matching and buyer alerts
stages.detail: Normalize Airtable inventory records, deduplicate owner and asset identities, maintain HubSpot buyer segments, and route relevant alerts. Measure qualified matches and buyer replies rather than counting raw messages.

stages.label: Transaction coordinator
stages.value: One contractor seat owns documents and independent settlement reconciliation
stages.detail: Track lien searches, creditor documents, signatures, inspection acceptance, and escrow statements. Require separate verification of changed payment instructions; the person entering a new bank destination must not be its sole verifier.

diagrams.title: A $60,000 Asset-Light Startup Allocation
diagrams.subtitle: Four cash buckets fit inside the canonical $10,000–$75,000 startup range.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are USD allocations totaling $60,000. This is one illustrative capitalization plan, not a prescribed minimum. Cash reserves are not immediate expenses; spending enters the appropriate operating category when incurred. Do not add these allocations again to the annual expense waterfall.
diagrams.caption: $36,000 + $8,000 + $10,000 + $6,000 = $60,000. The $36,000 recurring-overhead reserve covers nine months at $4,000 monthly before revenue, matching the upper end of the canonical two-to-nine-month first-deal window. Other spending uses the remaining buckets and must be paced separately.

stages.label: Recurring-overhead reserve
stages.value: $36,000 reserved for nine months of recurring operations
stages.detail: Hold this cash against the Base overhead assumption of $4,000 monthly. It excludes owner household spending and variable closing costs. Track actual runway weekly because late commissions can arrive after bills fall due.

stages.label: Field verification capacity
stages.value: $8,000 allocated to early inspections and ownership evidence
stages.detail: Fund initial specialist inspections, title and filing searches, equipment photography, and necessary site visits. Require asset-specific scopes and stop spending when a seller cannot establish authority or access.

stages.label: Seller and buyer acquisition
stages.value: $10,000 allocated to targeted sourcing and qualified outreach
stages.detail: Support focused trade-directory research, targeted seller outreach, buyer qualification, and selected industry visits. Release spending in small batches against mandate and buyer-match evidence rather than committing the full budget to broad advertising.

stages.label: Systems and transaction setup
stages.value: $6,000 allocated to equipment records and settlement readiness
stages.detail: Configure Airtable asset records, HubSpot workflows, document templates, e-signature, and secure file access. Establish escrow-provider verification and bookkeeping categories. Purchase no equipment inventory and advance no buyer purchase principal from this allocation.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to a Documented Brokerage Pipeline
diagrams.subtitle: Four weekly milestones build readiness; the first deal can take two to nine months.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are milestone end days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. Activity counts are sprint targets, not observed outcomes. A first-month settlement is not assumed, and the annual Base funnel is not compressed into this 30-day schedule.
diagrams.caption: Finish the sprint with a narrow equipment thesis, auditable asset records, qualified buyer conversations, and a rehearsed settlement process. Preserve cash for the canonical two-to-nine-month first-deal window instead of funding the business from an assumed first-month commission.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Select one niche and establish operating and evidence requirements
stages.detail: Choose a specific equipment class and geography. Complete a licensing activity matrix, seller mandate template, inspection checklist, and $60,000 cash plan. Assign the four Base seats and create Airtable fields for serial number, owner, condition, liens, and price.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Build twenty screened records and pursue five documented mandates
stages.detail: Target 20 distinct seller opportunities and five signed mandates with verified authority and evidence access. Establish independent inspection coverage and a lien-search workflow. Keep unsigned opportunities separate from inventory authorized for advertising.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Qualify ten buyer conversations and test three asset matches
stages.detail: Target ten conversations with identified purchasing decision-makers and three asset-specific matches. Record capacity, budget, location, and purchase timing. Test HubSpot buyer alerts against relevant inventory and retain explicit reasons for rejected matches.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Rehearse settlement and publish a cash-aware pipeline review
stages.detail: Walk one candidate transaction through inspection acceptance, creditor payoff, release documents, escrow instructions, and commission reconciliation. Use a simulation if no transaction is ready. Review cohort counts, blocked evidence, cash runway, and the next month's seller and buyer follow-up commitments.
